#Upload data
```{r}
load("otus_LCT_AllSamples_final.RData")
ASV <- as.matrix(otus)

taxa <- as.matrix(read.table("taxonomy_LCT_AllSamples_final.txt", sep = "\t", row.names = 1, header = TRUE))

ASV_ID <-read.table("ASVsequences_LCT_AllSamples_final.txt", sep = "\t", row.names = 1, header = TRUE)

metadata <- read.csv("Meta_Data.csv", header = TRUE)
rownames(metadata) <- metadata$sample_names
```


----------------------------------------------------
#Make base phyloseq object
```{r}
ASV = otu_table(ASV, taxa_are_rows = FALSE)
TAX = tax_table(taxa)
META = sample_data(metadata)

ps <- phyloseq(ASV, TAX, META) %>%
  filter_taxa(function(x) sum(x) > 0, prune = TRUE)

```

##### ASVs per sample
```{r}
#To find the number of ASVs per sample, but including the ASV multiple times in one sample
  otu_afterdada2 <- as.data.frame(otu_table(ps))
  otu_afterdada2$after_dada2_sum <- rowSums(otu_afterdada2)
  otu_afterdada2$sample_names <- rownames(otu_afterdada2)
  mean(otu_afterdada2$after_dada2_sum)  #60777.75
  sd(otu_afterdada2$after_dada2_sum) #80512.08
#To find the number of unique ASVs per sample (i.e. ASVs with count > 0)
  otu_afterdada2$unique_ASVs <- rowSums(otu_afterdada2 > 0)
  mean(otu_afterdada2$unique_ASVs) #646
  sd(otu_afterdada2$unique_ASVs) #646.2636
#
#Get the average number of ASVs from MiSeq and MiSeq i100. First I need to get the meta data and otu_afterdada2 in the same order (via sample_names)
  otu_meta_afterdada2 <- left_join(metadata, otu_afterdada2, by = "sample_names")
  cleaned_afterdada2 <- otu_meta_afterdada2 %>% select(-starts_with("ASV"))
# number of ASVs per sample, but including the ASV multiple times in one sample
  cleaned_afterdada2 %>% summarise(
    mean_MiSeqi100 = mean(after_dada2_sum[Library_ID == "Z2"], na.rm = TRUE),
    SD_MiSeqi100 = sd(after_dada2_sum[Library_ID == "Z2"], na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_MiSeq = mean(after_dada2_sum[Library_ID != "Z2"], na.rm = TRUE),
    SD_MiSeq = sd(after_dada2_sum[Library_ID != "Z2"], na.rm = TRUE))
          #   mean_MiSeqi100 SD_MiSeqi100 mean_MiSeq SD_MiSeq
          #        249794.2     105733.7   50158.85  64276.38
# To find the number of unique ASVs per sample (i.e. ASVs with count > 0)
  cleaned_afterdada2 %>% summarise(
    mean_MiSeqi100 = mean(unique_ASVs[Library_ID == "Z2"], na.rm = TRUE),
    SD_MiSeqi100 = sd(unique_ASVs[Library_ID == "Z2"], na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_MiSeq = mean(unique_ASVs[Library_ID != "Z2"], na.rm = TRUE),
    SD_MiSeq = sd(unique_ASVs[Library_ID != "Z2"], na.rm = TRUE),)
    #   mean_MiSeqi100 SD_MiSeqi100 mean_MiSeq SD_MiSeq
    #            1322     777.9457   608.0225 618.1739

#number of MiSeq i100 samples:
nrow(metadata[metadata$Library_ID == "Z2", ]) #15
#number of MiSeq samples:
nrow(metadata[metadata$Library_ID != "Z2", ]) #267
  
```


##### Rarefy i100 samples
```{r}
# Extract sample data and identify Z2 samples
z2_samples <- rownames(metadata[metadata$Library_ID == "Z2", ])
non_z2_samples <- rownames(metadata[metadata$Library_ID != "Z2", ])

# Subset phyloseq object
ps_z2 <- prune_samples(z2_samples, ps)
    # 15 samples
    # 65089 ASVs
ps_non_z2 <- prune_samples(non_z2_samples, ps)
    # 267 samples
    # 65089 ASVs
  quicklook <- as.data.frame(sample_sums(ps_non_z2))
  rm(quicklook)  
   
# Rarefy Z2 samples to 50159 reads
set.seed(18)  # for reproducibility
ps_z2_rarefied <- rarefy_even_depth(ps_z2, sample.size = 50159, rngseed = 18, verbose = FALSE)
    # 14 samples
    # 12548 ASVs

setdiff(sample_names(ps_z2), sample_names(ps_z2_rarefied)) #dropped Neg_Z2
sample_sums(ps_z2) #this is because Neg_Z2 had 24218 reads, which is less than 50159. 

#double check it worked
reads_per_sample <- sample_sums(ps_z2_rarefied)
reads_per_sample #everything is 50159! so that's good

# Combine back both parts
ps_rarefied <- merge_phyloseq(ps_non_z2, ps_z2_rarefied)
  # 281 samples
  # 65089 ASVs
otu.rarefied <- as.data.frame(otu_table(ps_rarefied))
otu.rarefied$rarefied_sum <- rowSums(otu.rarefied)
otu.rarefied["Neg_Z2", ] <- NA
mean(otu.rarefied$rarefied_sum, na.rm = TRUE) #50158.86

```


#Filter base phyloseq object
```{r}
#remove contaminants
load("contam.RData")
nrow(contam[contam$contaminant == "TRUE", ]) #148
 
ps.decontam <- prune_taxa(!contam$contaminant, ps_rarefied)
  # 281 samples
  # 64941 ASVs
otu.decontam <- as.data.frame(otu_table(ps.decontam))
otu.decontam$decontam_sum <- rowSums(otu.decontam)
otu.decontam["Neg_Z2", ] <- NA

#remove Mitochondria and Chloroplast
ps.nomitochloro <- ps.decontam %>%
    subset_taxa(Family !="Mitochondria" & Order !="Chloroplast")
       # 281 samples
       # 61665 ASVs
 otu.nomitochloro <- as.data.frame(otu_table(ps.nomitochloro))
 otu.nomitochloro$no_mitochloro_sum <- rowSums(otu.nomitochloro)
 otu.nomitochloro$unique_ASVs <- rowSums(otu.nomitochloro > 0)
 mean(otu.nomitochloro$unique_ASVs) #599.7046
 otu.nomitochloro["Neg_Z2", ] <- NA

#make a dataframe with the row sums (aka total reads) after each step 

reads_through_steps <- as.data.frame(cbind("sample_names1" = otu_afterdada2$sample_names,
                                     "Reads_After_Dada2" = otu_afterdada2$after_dada2_sum,
                                     "sample_names2" = rownames(otu.rarefied),
                                     "Reads_After_Rarefy" = otu.rarefied$rarefied_sum,
                                     "sample_names3" = rownames(otu.decontam),
                                     "Reads_After_Decontam" = otu.decontam$decontam_sum,
                                     "sample_names4" = rownames(otu.nomitochloro),
                                     "Reads_After_NoMitoChloro" = otu.nomitochloro$no_mitochloro_sum))


write.csv(reads_through_steps, "reads_through_steps.csv")
```


```{r}
## Remove samples with reads less than 10,000 and the unknown samples
ps.filtered <- ps.nomitochloro %>%
  prune_samples(sample_sums(.) > 9981, .) %>%
  filter_taxa(function(x) sum(x) > 0, prune = TRUE) #remove taxa with zero abundance 
    # 229 samples
    # 59348 ASVså

## Number of reads from the samples removed due to low read yield:
sample_reads <- sample_sums(ps.nomitochloro)
removed_samples <- names(sample_reads[sample_reads <= 9981])
removed_sample_df <- as.data.frame(sample_reads[removed_samples])


#To find the number of ASVs per sample, but including the ASV multiple times in one sample
  otu_ps.filtered <- as.data.frame(otu_table(ps.filtered))
  otu_ps.filtered$after_dada2_sum <- rowSums(otu_ps.filtered)
  otu_ps.filtered$sample_names <- rownames(otu_ps.filtered)
  sum(otu_ps.filtered$after_dada2_sum) #11875479
  mean(otu_ps.filtered$after_dada2_sum)  #51857.99
  sd(otu_ps.filtered$after_dada2_sum) #51872.93
#To find the number of unique ASVs per sample (i.e. ASVs with count > 0)
  otu_ps.filtered$unique_ASVs <- rowSums(otu_ps.filtered > 0)
  mean(otu_ps.filtered$unique_ASVs) #709.5153
  sd(otu_ps.filtered$unique_ASVs) #624.7191


#samples that were removed:
low_read_samples <- as.data.frame(sample_names(ps.nomitochloro)[sample_sums(ps.nomitochloro) <= 9981])
write.csv(low_read_samples, "low_read_samples.csv")
```

So this is 52 samples removed due to low read yield (below 9,982 reads).
Of these, 29 are negative controls and 23 are samples. 
All of the samples that are being removed are from Libraries V2 and Y2. This might not mean anything, but I am noting it. 
There are 33 negative controls, 5 mocks, and 244 samples in this data set.
If I remove these 23 samples, I will still have 221 samples left in my data set to work with. I think this is likely enough. 
The samples being removed include 16 coral samples, 6 mucus samples, and 1 water sample. I think this is within the realm of normal expectations. 

#Data evenness
```{r}

ps.nocontrol <- ps.filtered %>%
  subset_samples(Sample_Type != "Control") %>%
  subset_samples(Sample_Type != "Mock") %>%
  subset_samples(Sample_Type != "Water") %>%
  filter_taxa(function(x) sum(x) > 0, TRUE) %>%
  transform_sample_counts(function(x) x / sum(x)) #this makes everything in relative abundances


meta_filtered <- sample_data(ps.nocontrol)

data <- meta_filtered %>%
  group_by(Treatment, Site, Sample_Type) %>%
  summarize(freq = n())

ggplot(data, aes(x = Treatment, 
                 y = freq, 
                 fill = Site, 
                 group = interaction(Site, Sample_Type),
                 pattern = Sample_Type)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("lightseagreen", "magenta4")) +
  geom_bar_pattern(stat = "identity", 
                   position = position_dodge(width = 0.9),
                   pattern_fill = "black",
                   pattern_density = 0.3,
                   pattern_spacing = 0.03,
                   pattern_key_scale_factor = 0.5) +
  scale_pattern_manual(values = c("Mucus" = "stripe", "Tissue" = "none")) +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    text = element_text(size = 15),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 15)
  ) +
  labs(x = "", y = "Number of samples") +
  geom_text(aes(y = freq, label = freq), 
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), 
            vjust = -0.3, size = 4) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c(
    "Mesophotic initial",
    "Mesophotic to mesophotic",
    "Mesophotic to shallow",
    "Shallow initial",
    "Shallow to mesophotic",
    "Shallow to shallow"
  ))
```

#Survivorship
Did some excel calculations with these outputs, which can be found in: 
~/Documents/WHOI/Projects/LittleCaymanTransplant/Data_Analyses/Survivorship_data.xlsx
```{r}
#I need a different meta data for this, because the double outplanting at coral city shallow means that some of the survivorship data is lost in my current meta data. Because I would need two lines per initial coral for fate. 

Survivorship_data <- read.csv("Survivorship_data.csv", header = TRUE)

total_check <- Survivorship_data %>%
  dplyr::count(Treatment)
rm(total_check)
  
Fate_counts <- Survivorship_data %>%
  dplyr::count(Treatment, Fate)

Fate_percent <- Fate_counts %>%
  group_by(Treatment) %>%
  mutate(percent = n / sum(n) * 100)



ggplot(Fate_percent, aes(x = Treatment, y = percent, fill = Fate)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "stack") +
  labs(y = "Percent of corals",
       x = "",
       fill = "Fate") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("grey", "darkblue")) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank())


```



#PCoAs  
##### Sample Type
rm(list = setdiff(ls(), c("ps.filtered", "metadata")))

Phyloseq objects with counts so that I can centered log ratio transform them

```{r}
#All samples
ps.NoControl <- ps.filtered %>%
  subset_samples(Sample_Type != "Control") %>% #remove controls
  subset_samples(Sample_Type != "Mock") %>% #remove controls
  filter_taxa(function(x) sum(x) > 0, TRUE) #remove ASVS with all zeros

# transform the data
ps.NoControl.clr <- microbiome::transform(ps.NoControl, 'clr') #clr = centered log ratio
ord.NoControl.clr <- ordinate(ps.NoControl.clr, "RDA", "euclidean", set.seed(18))
plot_ordination(ps.NoControl.clr, ord.NoControl.clr , type="samples", color="Sample_Type") +
  geom_point(size = 4) +
  theme(text=element_text(size=14), panel.grid = element_blank()) +
  labs(title = "All samples with no controls")

            Permanova_metadata <- data.frame(sample_data(ps.NoControl.clr))
            perm <- adonis2(distance(ps.NoControl.clr, method="euclidean") ~ Sample_Type,
                    data = Permanova_metadata, 
                    permutations = how(blocks = Permanova_metadata$Site))
            perm

            rm(Permanova_metadata)
            rm(perm)

```

#Alpha diversity 
rm(list = setdiff(ls(), c("ps.filtered", "metadata")))
```{r}
#Need counts, not relative abundance
ps.NoControl_counts <- ps.filtered %>%
  subset_samples(Sample_Type != "Control") %>% #remove controls
  subset_samples(Sample_Type != "Mock") %>% #remove controls
  subset_samples(Sample_Type != "Water") %>%
  filter_taxa(function(x) sum(x) > 0, TRUE) #remove ASVS with all zeros
```


```{r}
allAlpha <- plot_richness(ps.NoControl_counts, x = "Treatment", measures = c("Observed","Chao1", "Shannon"))

alpha_Data <- allAlpha$data 
alpha_split <-split(alpha_Data, alpha_Data$variable)

#Observed is richness
alpha_Observed <- alpha_split$Observed
alpha_Observed_tissue <- alpha_Observed %>% filter(Sample_Type == "Tissue")
alpha_Observed_mucus <- alpha_Observed %>% filter(Sample_Type == "Mucus")
```

##### Tissue
```{r}
########################################################################
# Tissue
# Plot Observed (richness)

ggplot(alpha_Observed_tissue, aes(x = Treatment, y = value, color = Treatment)) +
   geom_jitter(width = 0.15, alpha = 0.6, size = 0.5) +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    text = element_text(size = 14),
    legend.position = "none") +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", size = 3) +
  stat_summary(
    fun.min = function(x) mean(x) - sd(x),
    fun.max = function(x) mean(x) + sd(x),
    geom = "errorbar",
    width = 0.1) +
  labs(x = "Treatment", y = "Richness",
       title = "Alpha diversity - Richness - Tissue") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("dodgerblue2", "dodgerblue4", "powderblue", "orchid2", "orchid4", "pink"))

########################################################################

#testing

######## for observed
lmer_mod <- lmer(value ~ Treatment + (1 | Outplant_rack), data = alpha_Observed_tissue)
lmer_mod
summary(lmer_mod)


confint(lmer_mod)



emm <- emmeans(lmer_mod, ~ Treatment)
pairs(emm, adjust = "tukey")


rm(lmer_mod)
rm(emm)
```

#Beta diversity 
useful resource on beta div types: https://docs.onecodex.com/en/articles/4150649-beta-diversity
Code based on Anya's from Cleanerfish project 

rm(list = setdiff(ls(), c("ps.filtered", "metadata")))

##### Tissue
```{r}
#phyloseq with only tissue, all sample treatments, both sites, no controls
ps.Tissue <- ps.filtered %>%
  subset_samples(Sample_Type == "Tissue") %>% 
  filter_taxa(function(x) sum(x) > 0, TRUE) #remove ASVS with all zeros

#Check
unique(sample_data(ps.Tissue)$Sample_Type)

ps.Tissue.clr <- microbiome::transform(ps.Tissue, 'clr') #clr = centered log ratio

otu_clr <- as.data.frame(otu_table(ps.Tissue.clr)) #pull out OTU table, make sure sample names are rows
metadat_clr <- as.data.frame(sample_data(ps.Tissue.clr)) #pull out Meta table
#Check if my rows are in the same order
identical(rownames(otu_clr), rownames(metadat_clr))
    #True!


Veg <- vegdist(otu_clr, method="euclidean") 


Mod_BetaDisp <-betadisper(Veg, metadat_clr$Treatment)
Mod_BetaDisp
summary(Mod_BetaDisp)

```


```{r}
##Prepare for plotting 

dist.tab <- as.data.frame(Mod_BetaDisp$distances)
dist.tab$Sample_names <- rownames(dist.tab)
colnames(dist.tab)[1] <- "distance"

identical(rownames(metadat_clr), dist.tab$Sample_names)
    #TRUE

dist.tab$Treatment <- metadat_clr$Treatment
dist.tab$Outplant_rack <- metadat_clr$Outplant_rack
dist.tab$Site <- metadat_clr$Site
dist.tab$Coral_ID <- metadat_clr$Coral_ID
dist.tab$Sample_Type <- metadat_clr$Sample_Type
dist.tab


ggplot(dist.tab, aes(x = Treatment, y = distance, color = Treatment)) +
   geom_jitter(width = 0.15, alpha = 0.6, size = 0.5) +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    text = element_text(size = 14),
    legend.position = "none") +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", size = 3) +
  stat_summary(
    fun.min = function(x) mean(x) - sd(x),
    fun.max = function(x) mean(x) + sd(x),
    geom = "errorbar",
    width = 0.1) +
  labs(x = "", y = "Distance to centroid",
       title = "Beta diversity - Tissue") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("dodgerblue2", "dodgerblue4", "powderblue", "orchid2", "orchid4", "pink"))
```


```{r}
#testing

lmer_mod <- lmer(distance ~ Treatment + (1 | Outplant_rack), data = dist.tab)
lmer_mod
summary(lmer_mod)


confint(lmer_mod)


emm <- emmeans(lmer_mod, ~ Treatment)
pairs(emm, adjust = "tukey")
 

```

# 10% - All treatment bar plots
##### Tissue

```{r}
rm(list = setdiff(ls(), c("ps.filtered", "metadata")))

ps.AllTreat.Tissue <- ps.filtered %>%
  subset_samples(Sample_Type == "Tissue") %>% 
  filter_taxa(function(x) sum(x) > 0, TRUE) %>% #remove ASVS with all zeros
  transform_sample_counts(function(x) x / sum(x) ) #this makes everything in relative abundances

#Check that it's relative abundance
otu_table(ps.AllTreat.Tissue)[1:3, 1:3]

AllTreat_data <- psmelt(ps.AllTreat.Tissue)
names(AllTreat_data)[1] <- "ASV"
AllTreat_data$ASV_GenusSpecies <- paste(AllTreat_data$ASV, AllTreat_data$Genus, AllTreat_data$Species, sep = " ") # make a new variable with ASV, Genus, and Species
AllTreat_data <- AllTreat_data[AllTreat_data$Abundance != 0, ] #remove if ASV abundance is zero

#select genera that are >1% in any sample
top_by_sample <- AllTreat_data %>%
  filter(Abundance > 0.1) %>%
  distinct(Genus)

# Filter original long data to keep only those Treatment-specific top genera
filtered_Genus <- AllTreat_data %>%
  inner_join(top_by_sample %>% select(Genus),
             by = c("Genus"))

# How many genera per treatment did we keep?
filtered_Genus %>%
  dplyr::distinct(Treatment, Genus) %>%
  dplyr::count(Treatment)
# How many total genera?
length(unique(filtered_Genus$Genus)) #27
#Get the full unique taxonomy in decreasing abundance
unique_taxonomy_ordered <- filtered_Genus %>%
  group_by(Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus) %>%
  summarise(Total_Abundance = sum(Abundance, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(Total_Abundance))

# Set factor to genera are in order of decreasing abundance
filtered_Genus$Genus <- factor(filtered_Genus$Genus,
                                levels = unique_taxonomy_ordered$Genus)

# write.csv(unique_taxonomy_ordered, "unique_taxonomy_ordered_Tissue.csv")

#Get my color scheme
unique_taxonomy_ordered_colors_tissue <- read.csv("unique_taxonomy_ordered_colors_tissue.csv")
color_map <- setNames(unique_taxonomy_ordered_colors_tissue$Color, 
                      unique_taxonomy_ordered_colors_tissue$Genus)

Top10PercentGenre_AllTreat_Tissue <- ggplot(filtered_Genus, aes(x = Sample, y = Abundance, fill = Genus)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") + 
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), 
        text=element_text(size=20),
        axis.text.x = element_blank(), 
        axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 16),
        legend.title=element_blank(),
        legend.position = "bottom") +
  labs(x = "", y = bquote("Relative abundance")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = color_map) +
  facet_grid(~ Treatment, scales="free", space="free")

Top10PercentGenre_AllTreat_Tissue +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

```

##### Tissue

```{r}
rm(list = setdiff(ls(), c("ps.filtered", "metadata")))

ps.AllTreat.Tissue <- ps.filtered %>%
  subset_samples(Sample_Type == "Tissue") %>% 
  filter_taxa(function(x) sum(x) > 0, TRUE) %>% #remove ASVS with all zeros
  transform_sample_counts(function(x) x / sum(x) ) #this makes everything in relative abundances

#Check that it's relative abundance
otu_table(ps.AllTreat.Tissue)[1:3, 1:3]

AllTreat_data <- psmelt(ps.AllTreat.Tissue)
names(AllTreat_data)[1] <- "ASV"
AllTreat_data$ASV_GenusSpecies <- paste(AllTreat_data$ASV, AllTreat_data$Genus, AllTreat_data$Species, sep = " ") # make a new variable with ASV, Genus, and Species

# these steps ID the top 40 genre per treatment to plot:
# Sum abundance within each Treatment x Genus, rank within Treatment, keep top 40
top40_by_treatment <- AllTreat_data %>%
  group_by(Treatment, Genus) %>%
  summarise(AbundanceSum = sum(Abundance), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(Treatment) %>%
  slice_max(order_by = AbundanceSum, n = 40, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup()

# Filter original long data to keep only those Treatment-specific top genera
filtered_Genus <- AllTreat_data %>%
  inner_join(top40_by_treatment %>% select(Treatment, Genus),
             by = c("Treatment", "Genus"))

# How many genera per treatment did we keep?
filtered_Genus %>%
  distinct(Treatment, Genus) %>%
  count(Treatment)
# How many total genera?
length(unique(filtered_Genus$Genus)) #77
#Get the full unique taxonomy in decreasing abundance
unique_taxonomy_ordered <- filtered_Genus %>%
  group_by(Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus) %>%
  summarise(Total_Abundance = sum(Abundance, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(Total_Abundance))

# Set factor to genera are in order of decreasing abundance
filtered_Genus$Genus <- factor(filtered_Genus$Genus,
                                levels = unique_taxonomy_ordered$Genus)

# write.csv(unique_taxonomy_ordered, "unique_taxonomy_ordered_Tissue.csv")

#Get my color scheme
unique_taxonomy_ordered_colors_tissue <- read_csv("unique_taxonomy_ordered_colors_tissue.csv")

Top40Genre_AllTreat_Tissue <- ggplot(filtered_Genus, aes(x = Sample, y = Abundance, fill = Genus)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") + 
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), 
        text=element_text(size=20),
        axis.text.x = element_blank(), 
        axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 16),
        legend.title=element_blank(),
        legend.position = "bottom") +
  labs(x = "", y = bquote("Relative abundance")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = unique_taxonomy_ordered_colors_tissue$Color) +
  facet_grid(~ Treatment, scales="free", space="free")

Top40Genre_AllTreat_Tissue +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

#Differential abundance
Corncob method

##### Initial Tissue
rm(list = setdiff(ls(), c("ps.filtered")))
```{r}
#Corncob wants count data, not relative abundance.

#phyloseq object with count data, not relative abundance

ps.endo <- ps.filtered %>%
           subset_samples(Sample_Type == "Tissue") %>% 
           subset_samples(Timepoint == "Initial") %>% 
           subset_taxa(grepl("Endozoicomonas", Genus) & !grepl("Kistimonas", Genus)) %>% 
           filter_taxa(function(x) sum(x) > 0, TRUE) #remove ASVS with all zeros 

#Double check that this is count data
otu_table(ps.endo)[1:3, 1:3]
#Double check that this is just Endozoicomonas
tax_table(ps.endo)[, "Genus"]

# Make factors
sample_data(ps.endo)$Treatment <-   factor(sample_data(ps.endo)$Treatment,levels=c("D0", "S0"))

# Corncob: Differential abundance test 
set.seed(1)
DA.Initial_Tissue <- differentialTest(formula = ~ Treatment + Site, 
                             phi.formula = ~ Treatment + Site,
                             formula_null = ~  + Site,
                             phi.formula_null = ~ Treatment + Site,
                             test = "Wald", boot = FALSE,
                             data = ps.endo,
                             fdr_cutoff = 0.05)
DA.Initial_Tissue$significant_taxa # "ASV1"   "ASV122" "ASV464"
length(DA.Initial_Tissue$significant_taxa) #3
DA.Initial_Tissue$significant_models

#make a df of the corncob output and the taxonomy
#This is from Cynthia's published code: https://github.com/CynthiaBecker/SCTLD-STT/blob/main/Code_to_Reproduce_Figures_in_Manuscript.Rmd
#Write a function to extract the significant taxa and put it in a dataframe with a for loop so you can rearrange the levels of the taxa to make a nice ordered graph. 

sigtaxto_df <- function(daout, psobj) {
  df.out <- c()
  for (i in 1:length(daout$significant_models)) { #from 1 to the number of significant taxa
  df.out = rbind(df.out, daout$significant_models[[i]]$coefficients[2, 1:4]) #bind the sig.mcav row with coefficient, std. error, t value, Pr thing. coefficients[2,] is the DA model output.
  }
  asv = as.vector(daout$significant_taxa) #get significant ASVs
  Class = as.vector(otu_to_taxonomy(data = psobj, daout$significant_taxa, level = c("Class"))) #isolate class of significant Asvs
  Order = as.vector(otu_to_taxonomy(data = psobj, daout$significant_taxa, level = c("Order"))) #isolate order of significant ASVs
  Family = as.vector(otu_to_taxonomy(data = psobj, daout$significant_taxa, level = c("Family"))) #isolate family of significant ASVs
  Family.fix = ifelse(Family == "", "unclassified", Family) #replace empty values with "unclassified"
  Genus = as.vector(otu_to_taxonomy(data = psobj, daout$significant_taxa, level = c("Genus"))) #isolate Genus of singnificant ASVs
  Genus.fix = ifelse(Genus == "", "unclassified", Genus) #replace empty values with "unclassified"
  
  df.bind <- as.data.frame(cbind(df.out, asv, Class, Order, Family.fix, Genus.fix)) #bind taxonomic info together, making sure to use the vectors with "unclassified"
  df.bind$asvgenus <- paste0(df.bind$Genus.fix, " (", df.bind$asv, ")") #make a concatenated column of ASV and Genus.
  colnames(df.bind) <- c("Estimate", "StdError", "tvalue", "Pr", "asv", "Class", "Order", "Family", "Genus", "asvtaxa")
  df.bind$Estimate = as.numeric(as.character(df.bind$Estimate)) #estimate column should be numeric 
  df.bind$StdError = as.numeric(as.character(df.bind$StdError)) #stderror column should be numeric 
  
  return(df.bind)
}

Taxa.forgraph <- sigtaxto_df(DA.Initial_Tissue, ps.endo) 
#write.csv(Taxa.forgraph, "DATaxa_Initial_Tissue.csv")

ggplot(Taxa.forgraph, aes(x = asvtaxa, y = Estimate)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = Estimate-StdError, ymax = Estimate+StdError), color = "black", width = .3, position=position_dodge(.9)) +
  geom_point(size = 4, pch = 21, color="black", fill="black") + 
  scale_x_discrete(limits = rev(levels(Taxa.forgraph$asvtaxa))) +
  geom_line() +
  coord_flip() +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "Taxa", y = "Coefficient", title = expression(italic("S0 vs D0"))) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "darkgray")
```

```{r}
# plot treatment differences

# I need to do this, because some corals have two of the same treatment, because CC Shallow corals didn't get properly crossed. Both halves went  to the same depth. 
df_clean <- qPCR_tissue %>%
  group_by(Coral_ID, Treatment, Site, Sample_Type) %>%
  summarise(Log10_Copies = mean(Log10_Copies), .groups = "drop")


df_wide <- df_clean %>%
  select(Coral_ID, Treatment, Log10_Copies, Site, Sample_Type) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from  = Treatment,
    values_from = Log10_Copies)

df_diff <- df_wide %>%
  mutate(DS_minus_D0 = DS - D0,
         DD_minus_D0 = DD - D0,
         SD_minus_S0 = SD - S0,
         SS_minus_S0 = SS - S0) %>%
  select(Coral_ID, Site, Sample_Type, DS_minus_D0, DD_minus_D0, SD_minus_S0, SS_minus_S0)

diff_long <- df_diff %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -c(Coral_ID, Site, Sample_Type),      # columns to keep
    names_to = "Treatment",       # new column containing the names
    values_to = "difference_in_Log10Endo"       # new column containing the values
  )

diff_SDandDS <- diff_long %>%
                 filter(Treatment %in% c("DS_minus_D0", "SD_minus_S0"))

ggplot(diff_SDandDS, aes(x = Treatment, y = Coral_ID, fill = difference_in_Log10Endo)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c() +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "red",        # negative values
    mid = "white",      # zero
    high = "blue",      # positive values
    midpoint = 0        # center of the scale
  ) 



```

```{r}
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 16),
        legend.title=element_blank(),
        legend.position = "bottom") +
  labs(x = "", y = bquote("Relative abundance")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = myColor) +
  facet_grid( ~ Origin_Depth_DS, scales="free", space="free")

Top40Genre_water + 
   theme(legend.position = "")


```


#### qPCR Endo
rm(list = setdiff(ls(), c("ps.filtered", "metadata")))
```{r}
qPCR_Water <- metadata %>%
  filter(Sample_Type == "Water") %>%
  filter(Site %in% c("Coral_City", "Marthas_Finyard")) %>%
  mutate(Treatment = factor(Treatment,
                  levels = c("S",
                             "D")))
unique(qPCR_Water$Sample_Type)
unique(qPCR_Water$Site)

qPCR_Water$Norm_Copies <- qPCR_Water$Endo_Avg_Quantity/qPCR_Water$DNA_Concentration
qPCR_Water$Log10_Copies <- log10(qPCR_Water$Norm_Copies)      # remember in R that log() = natural log (base e)
```


```{r}
# Plot mean ± SD

#Make the samples collected at 20 m as S
qPCR_Water$Origin_Depth_DS[qPCR_Water$Origin_Depth_DS == "M"] <- "S"
unique(qPCR_Water$Origin_Depth_DS)

#summarize Abundance by depth
qPCR_Water_summary <- qPCR_Water %>%
  group_by(Origin_Depth_DS) %>%
  summarize(
    mean_LOGabundance = mean(Log10_Copies, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_LOGabundance = sd(Log10_Copies, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_NORMabundance = mean(Norm_Copies, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_NORMabundance = sd(Norm_Copies, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop")


```


```{r}
# testing
aov_mod <- aov(Log10_Copies ~ Origin_Depth_DS * Site, data = qPCR_Water)
summary(aov_mod)
    

```


```{r}
ggplot() +
   geom_jitter(data =  qPCR_Water,  aes(x = Origin_Depth_DS, y = Log10_Copies),  
     width = 0.15, alpha = 0.6, size = 4,  color = "black") +
  geom_errorbar(data =  qPCR_Water_summary, 
                aes(x = Origin_Depth_DS, 
                    ymin = mean_LOGabundance - sd_LOGabundance,
                    ymax = mean_LOGabundance + sd_LOGabundance),
                width = 0.2) +
  geom_point(data =  qPCR_Water_summary,  aes(x = Origin_Depth_DS, y = mean_LOGabundance, fill = Origin_Depth_DS),
    shape = 22, size = 11, color = "black") +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    text = element_text(size = 14),
    legend.position = "none"
  ) +
  ylim(0,4) +
  labs(x = "Treatment", y = "Quantity (log[copies/ng])",
       title = "Endozoicomonas absolute abundance (mean ± SD)") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("dodgerblue2", "orchid2"))
```
